column1: # Tour three-mode executor contract — the single source of truth for the exact
# argv, stage decomposition and body-execution policy of every (applicability,
# mode) pair in the pinned tour executable denominator.
# Sprint 118 / Story #4 / Story-ID 759341a95870.
# tools/tour/executor.rb builds commands ONLY from these rows and
# tools/tour/executor-gate.rb re-derives the expected argv from the same rows,
# so the producer and the offline gate can never drift into checking a
# different command than the one that actually ran. The contract's SHA-256 is
# pinned into every produced ledger's manifest.
# Corrections this contract encodes over the superseded tour-evidence/v2 runner
# (tools/tour/evidence.rb, retained unchanged with its historical failure
# evidence in tests/tour/evidence.jsonl):
#   1. `bashy transpile` invoked WITHOUT `--bashpp` — rejected by
#      bashy/internal/agentos/transpile.go ("transpile: --bashpp is required").
#      Both Bash++ modes now carry the explicit Go-source selector
#      `--source=go` from the sprint-118 plan §2.7, so an original .go file is
#      ingested as Go and never as shell.
#   2. Build-only rows were driven with `-n` (parse only) in interpreted mode
#      and their compiled pipeline unconditionally executed the artifact.
#      Parsing cannot establish buildability and a `norun` row must not have
#      its body executed. Interpreted build-only now uses the semantic-check
#      selector `--check`; compiled build-only stops after `build`.
#   3. The Go baseline for an applicable row is `go build` + execution of the
#      NATIVE ARTIFACT, never `go run`. `go run`'s wrapper exit status can
#      misreport os.Exit and panics, so comparing it against a native product
#      exit misclassifies those rows (sprint-118 plan §5). This is also the
#      exact recipe that produced the accepted observations in
#      tests/tour/results.tsv (tools/tour/run-baseline.sh), so the executor's
#      fresh baseline and the pinned accepted baseline are comparable.
#   4. The compiled pipeline records three SEPARATE stages, each with its own
#      argv, status and declared artifacts (including the transpiler source
#      map), so a successful transpile can never masquerade as a successful
#      artifact run.
# `phase` is the CURRENT executor phase contract. For the applicable class it
# is identical to the pinned differential-schema token. For the four build-only
# rows the pinned tokens (`go-test-or-build`, `parse-or-run`,
# `transpile-build-run`) all contain a `run` the master execution plan forbids
# for a norun row, so this contract states the honest no-body phase instead and
# docs/tour/phase-migration.tsv is the checked bridge back to the pinned
# historical string. The inventory itself is untouched; the gate enforces both
# ends of that table.
# Process environment (fixed by tools/tour/executor-runner.rb, recorded per
# stage): GOMAXPROCS=2 in every mode (including native oracle repeats);
# LC_ALL=C — matching tools/tour/run-baseline.sh, which produced the
# accepted observations; GOTOOLCHAIN=local; GOFLAGS=-mod=mod; GOPROXY=off after
# helper provisioning; BASHY_HINTS=off; a FRESH HOME and TMPDIR per (row, mode);
# and a freshly materialized read-only module tree per mode. GOROOT names the
# pinned SDK and is supplied IDENTICALLY to all three modes: the product's Go
# import bridge resolves stdlib packages through it, so withholding it from one
# mode would compare different environments, not different engines.
# PATH is /usr/bin:/bin for toolchain stages (`{GO}` invocations) and EMPTY for
# every stage that executes a tested body, so a typed-only tour program cannot
# reach an external command and no mode can silently acquire shell fallback.
# A `run` stage additionally executes from a FRESH, EMPTY runtime directory: the
# compilation inputs are moved to the durable artifact directory first, so the
# native artifact cannot read its own source out of the cwd. Interpreted mode
# necessarily keeps its module context, since the source IS its input. This is
# cwd and command-lookup isolation, NOT an OS-level denial — every stage records
# that exact scope and the gate rejects a stronger claim.
# ADJUDICATED (docs/tour/phase-migration.tsv): the build-only rows execute NO
# body in any mode. The pinned inventory strings are retained unchanged as
# historical schema and joined through the migration table, which the gate
# checks against both the inventory and this contract.
# Placeholders, substituted by the executor:
#   {GO}       absolute path to the pinned Go 1.27.0 binary (docs/tour/toolchain.tsv)
#   {BASHY}    absolute path to the candidate bashy launcher (docs/tour/candidate.tsv)
#   {SRC}      module-relative path of the original, unmodified upstream .go file
#   {OUT_GO}   transpiled Go artifact, in the per-mode artifact directory
#   {OUT_MAP}  transpiler source map artifact, in the per-mode artifact directory
#   {BIN}      built native artifact, in the per-mode artifact directory
# `produces` names the artifacts a stage must have created for it to count as
# successful; `-` means the stage produces no file artifact. `execute_body`
# records whether the stage runs the tested program's body: every `no` stage is
# a semantic/build obligation and the gate rejects a ledger in which such a
# stage produced any program output.
